## HAITI — profile (page 169)

- Header facts: Region: Latin America & the Caribbean; income group: Lower-middle-income; lending category: IDA; data status: Data as reported (A); population: 11.9 million; GNI: 32,083.8; unit line: US$ million, unless otherwise indicated.
- Total external debt stock 2025: 827.5, a change of -12.7% from 2024.

- Figure 1 Total external debt, 2015–25: 2,240.0 in 2015 and 827.5 in 2025. The line is broadly rising from 2015 through the early 2020s, reaching a peak around 2023 at ≈2.9 billion, staying near that level in 2024, and then falling sharply in 2025.

- Figure 2 External debt by creditor and creditor type in 2025, including IMF credit and SDR allocations:
  - Total external debt: 827.5

    - Private nonguaranteed: 7.7
    - Short-term: 33.1
  - Public & publicly guaranteed — by creditor type: 786.7
    - Multilateral: 607.6
    - Bilateral: 147.7
    - Private creditors: 31.4
  - Multilateral: 607.6
    - IMF-SDR allocations: 322.9
    - IMF credit: 221.8
    - Other multilateral: 62.9
  - Bilateral: 147.7
    - Multiple lenders: 120.9
    - Venezuela, RB: 26.8

- Figure 3 Debt ratios, 2015–25:
  - External debt / exports: 99%, change -6.2%. Trend: rises from 2015, peaks around 2022, then declines sharply by 2024 and edges lower in 2025.
  - External debt / GNI: 3%, change -34.0%. Trend: broadly low and fairly flat through most of the period, then declines noticeably in 2024–25.
  - Debt service / exports: 6%, change -90.2%. Trend: very low for most years, a sharp spike around 2024, then a steep drop in 2025.
  - Debt service / GNI: 0.2%, change -93.1%. Trend: low throughout, with a spike around 2024 followed by a sharp fall in 2025.
